title: Long usernames
prompt: A username is too long if it has more than 5 characters. Show the id of users with a username that's too long.
solutions: SELECT id FROM users WHERE LENGTH(username) > 5;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM users WHERE LENGTH(username) >= 5;
SELECT id FROM users WHERE username > 5;
wrongSolutions.why: Compares the text, not its length

title: Odd rows, not Maths
prompt: Show the title of courses with an odd id whose subject isn't Maths, sorted by title from Z to A.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (9, 'Art', 'Arts'), (11, 'Zoology', 'Science');

solutions: SELECT title FROM courses WHERE id % 2 = 1 AND subject <> 'Maths' ORDER BY title DESC;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title FROM courses WHERE id % 2 = 0 AND subject <> 'Maths' ORDER BY title DESC;
SELECT title FROM courses WHERE id % 2 = 1 AND subject <> 'Maths' ORDER BY title;

title: Award eligibility
prompt: An employee is eligible when they earn over 50000, have a recorded bonus, and were hired before 2022. Show each name and eligible as Yes or No.
hints: All three parts must be true.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary > 50000 AND bonus IS NOT NULL AND hire_date < '2022-01-01' THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS eligible FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary > 50000 OR bonus IS NOT NULL OR hire_date < '2022-01-01' THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS eligible FROM employees;
SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary > 50000 AND hire_date < '2022-01-01' THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS eligible FROM employees;

title: Study partners
prompt: Students pair up by id: an odd id works with the next id, and an even id with the previous one. Show each student's id and partner_id, sorted by id.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT id, CASE WHEN id % 2 = 1 THEN id + 1 ELSE id - 1 END AS partner_id FROM students ORDER BY id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, CASE WHEN id % 2 = 0 THEN id + 1 ELSE id - 1 END AS partner_id FROM students ORDER BY id;
SELECT id, id + 1 AS partner_id FROM students ORDER BY id;

title: Tidy city names
prompt: Show each customer's id and their name with the first letter in capitals and the rest lowercase, as tidy_name, sorted by id.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE customers SET name = 'mATEO' WHERE id = 2;

solutions: SELECT id, UPPER(SUBSTR(name, 1, 1)) || LOWER(SUBSTR(name, 2)) AS tidy_name FROM customers ORDER BY id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, UPPER(name) AS tidy_name FROM customers ORDER BY id;
SELECT id, name AS tidy_name FROM customers ORDER BY id;

title: Gold members
prompt: A gold tag is any tag starting with GOLD. Show the id, full_name, and tags of contacts with a gold tag, either first or after a space.
hints: Check the start and after a space.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: SELECT id, full_name, tags FROM contacts WHERE tags LIKE 'GOLD%' OR tags LIKE '% GOLD%';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, full_name, tags FROM contacts WHERE tags LIKE '%GOLD%';
SELECT id, full_name, tags FROM contacts WHERE tags LIKE 'GOLD%';
